sentences: On output stream zero, `GS_OP_EMIT_CUT` emits the staged vertex and ends its strip under the same EXEC guard.
The synthetic `gs_emit_cut.asm` checks that six vertices form two separate triangles. [RDNA 2 ISA, S_SENDMSG](https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/Et~wpu9g~Ffl7d9q0QZ~Og/content).
All 195 are `$GS_VoxelizeGeneric` permutations: legacy (merged ES/GS) wave32 programs on LDS rings, with no `exp`.

All 195 are `$GS_VoxelizeGeneric` permutations: legacy (merged ES/GS) programs on LDS rings, with no `exp`, written for wave64 (inferred from the code, not confirmed against the console's wave-size setting: the EXEC prologue that `gs_tri.asm` mirrors compares the thread count with 64 and writes a 64-bit EXEC, the count in #94 finds `v_mbcnt_hi_u32_b32` in all 195, and the translator marks all 195 `wave64`; an earlier version of this row said wave32, TEST-251).

Inputs: vertex i sits at the dword offset in v0 lo / v0 hi / v1 lo; an LDS read at vertex base + 4·(4·reg + comp) is input-signature register reg, component comp (checked: SV_Position xyz in dwords 0–2 and TEXCOORD0.xy in 4–5, as ISG1 declares).
Outputs: emitted vertex k is dwords [k·4·nreg, (k+1)·4·nreg) of the lane's GSVS area, dword = 4·reg + comp of the output signature (20 dwords = 5 OSG1 registers; every write matches a declared mask).

Translation: synthetic offsets (vertex i at dword 64·i), LDS reads → `gl_in[i]` inputs, LDS writes → staged slots, `MSG_GS EMIT` → copy slot (emit count) to the outputs + `OpEmitVertex`, `CUT` → `OpEndPrimitive`, `GS_DONE` → nothing.
The prologue's `s_bfm_b64`/`s_cselect` EXEC setup is fed s3 = 64 << 8.

Without a geometry stage (Apple GPUs: Metal, MoltenVK), `tools/spirv_gs_to_compute.py` lowers the translated module to a compute capture pass, one invocation per input primitive: inputs come from a buffer, each `OpEmitVertex` writes the outputs to a record buffer, and a meta buffer holds each primitive's vertex count and strip ends, for an ordinary draw afterwards (SHADER-159).

`gs_tri` lowered this way, converted with SPIRV-Cross and run natively on an Apple A18 Pro: 195/195 records exact for 65 random triangles, and the captured fullscreen triangle drawn from the records matches all 4096 gradient pixels.
Not done: wiring it into a draw path, and GS that use cross-lane operations or more than one invocation.
